cohort: The study included 17 female patients aged 30-59 years who underwent sling procedures for varying degrees of uterovaginal prolapse.
finding: Sling procedures were found to be effective and safe for treating uterovaginal prolapse, with high patient satisfaction and low complication rates.
cross-section timing: Data were collected retrospectively from case records between 2022 and 2024, assessing outcomes following sling procedures performed over a 2-year period.
